title: Best Air Fryers of 2026: Ninja, COSORI, Instant Vortex and More Reviewed
excerpt: Five air fryers for every kitchen and budget, from the compact Dash to the family-size COSORI and Philips XXL: who each one suits, how to choose the right size, and first-use tips.
html:
Air fryers have earned their place on the counter: they crisp frozen fries, wings and vegetables with a spoonful of oil or none, heat up faster than a full-size oven and are easy to clean. Choosing one is harder than using one, though. Sizes run from 2-quart baskets for one person to family-size drawers, and the extra functions, presets and price vary just as much.

This guide compares five air fryers for different kitchens and budgets: the Ninja AF101, the COSORI TurboBlaze 6-Quart, the Instant Vortex Plus from the makers of the Instant Pot, the Philips Premium Airfryer XXL and the Dash Compact. For each one you will find who it suits, its strengths and limits, and a buying guide to help you choose the right size.

Already have an air fryer? Our free oven to air fryer conversion calculator turns any oven recipe into air fryer time and temperature.

How We Chose These Air Fryers

We looked for air fryers that cover the needs of most US kitchens, from a single person in a studio apartment to a family of six, and judged each one on the points that matter in daily use.

1

Capacity for the household

How many people the basket can feed in one batch, and whether food fits in a single layer, which is what makes it crisp.

2

Temperature range and functions

A top temperature of at least 400°F for crisping, a low range for dehydrating, and extra functions only where they add real use.

3

Ease of cleaning

Nonstick, dishwasher-safe baskets and crisper plates, and few parts that trap grease.

4

Controls

Clear dials or touchscreens that make it easy to set the exact temperature and time a recipe calls for.

5

Footprint and value

How much counter space each model takes, and whether its features justify its price tier.

Detailed Reviews: The 5 Best Air Fryers

What each air fryer does well, where it falls short and who should buy it. Models are updated from time to time, so check the current version on the listing.

1
Best Overall

Ninja AF101 Air Fryer

Best for: Most households of one to four people who want a simple, dependable basket air fryer.

Check price on Amazon

The Ninja AF101 is a 4-quart basket air fryer with four functions: air fry, roast, reheat and dehydrate. Ninja lists a temperature range of 105°F to 400°F, which covers everything from crisping frozen fries at the top of the dial to drying fruit and jerky at the bottom.

The ceramic-coated nonstick basket and crisper plate go in the dishwasher, and Ninja says the basket holds about 2 pounds of french fries: a side dish for two to four people. The square body fits under most kitchen cabinets and leaves room on the counter.

It is also one of the most widely sold air fryers on Amazon, so replacement crisper plates, liners and recipes written for it are easy to find.

The trade-offs come with the size. A family of five or more will cook in batches, and there are no food presets: you choose the function, temperature and time yourself. Our oven to air fryer conversion calculator gives you exactly those two numbers for any oven recipe.

Pros

  • Four functions, including dehydrate
  • Wide 105°F to 400°F range
  • Ceramic-coated, dishwasher-safe basket and crisper plate
  • Compact footprint for small counters
  • Accessories and recipes are easy to find

Cons

  • 4-quart basket is small for large families
  • No food presets
  • One basket, so one food at a time

Verdict: The best all-round choice for most kitchens: simple to use, easy to clean and big enough for everyday meals for up to four.

Best for Families

COSORI TurboBlaze 6-Quart Air Fryer

Best for: Families and batch cooks who want room to spread food out in a single layer.

Check price on Amazon

COSORI’s 6-quart TurboBlaze model is built for bigger batches. COSORI lists nine cooking functions, including air fry, roast, bake, broil, dehydrate and proof, a top temperature of 450°F and a fan rated at 3,600 rpm with five speed settings.

The square basket uses its space better than a round one, so wings, drumsticks and fries can sit in a single layer, which is what makes them crisp instead of steamed. COSORI also rates it at under 53 decibels, quieter than many full-size models.

The basket has a PFAS-free ceramic nonstick coating, according to COSORI, and goes in the dishwasher. COSORI’s app adds more than 100 recipes for people who like step-by-step guidance.

It is more air fryer than a single cook needs, and it takes more counter space than a 4-quart model. The extra fan speeds and modes also take a little longer to learn.

Pros

  • Large square basket for family-size batches
  • Up to 450°F with adjustable fan speeds
  • Nine cooking functions
  • PFAS-free ceramic, dishwasher-safe basket
  • Rated quieter than many models

Cons

  • Bigger footprint on the counter
  • More capacity than one or two people need
  • More settings to learn

Verdict: Our pick for families: the large basket and high top temperature make big batches of crispy food easier.

Instant Vortex Plus 6-Quart Air Fryer

Best for: Instant Pot owners and anyone who prefers touchscreen controls with one-touch programs.

The Vortex line is the air fryer range from Instant Brands, the company behind the Instant Pot. The Vortex Plus 6-Quart is a six-function basket air fryer, with air fry, roast, bake, broil, dehydrate and reheat, a temperature range of 95°F to 400°F and a touchscreen control panel.

One-touch programs make it easy for anyone who likes to press a button and walk away, and the familiar Instant interface will feel natural if you already cook with an Instant Pot. The nonstick basket is dishwasher safe.

Instant sells the Vortex line in several sizes, from compact baskets to 10-quart air fryer ovens. This one is the 6-quart basket, a good size for three to five people.

It is bulkier than the 4-quart Ninja, and some owners find the preset programs need adjusting to their own taste: treat the presets as a starting point, just like any converted recipe.

Philips introduced the Airfryer in 2010, and the Premium XXL is its family-size model. Philips lists it at 7 quarts, enough for a whole chicken or about 3 pounds of fries.

Its Fat Removal technology separates excess fat from the food and collects it in the bottom of the drawer, so less of it ends up on the plate. Rapid Air circulation, a digital display with presets and a keep-warm mode round it out, and Philips says no preheating is needed.

The QuickClean basket and the removable parts are dishwasher safe.

It is a premium appliance: it costs more than the other picks, it is heavy, and it does fewer extra jobs than the multi-function models. Philips also updates its lineup regularly, so check the current listing for the exact version.

Verdict: The premium choice for large portions, with the extra benefit of collecting the fat that cooks out of food.

The limits are the ones you would expect at this size. There are no presets or extra functions, and anything for more than two people means cooking in batches.

Buying Guide: How to Choose the Best Air Fryer

1. Choose the right capacity

Air fryer capacity is measured in quarts. Buy for the way you cook most often: a basket that is too small means batches, and one that is too large wastes counter space and energy.

CapacityGood forTypical batch
2 quarts or less1 personSnacks, sides, reheating
3 to 4 quarts1 to 3 peopleAbout 2 lb of fries, 2 chicken breasts
5 to 6 quarts3 to 5 peopleA batch of wings, a small whole chicken
7 quarts and up, dual basket or oven style5 people or moreMain and side together, batch cooking

2. Basket, dual basket or oven style

Basket air fryers are the most common: a pull-out drawer with a perforated crisper plate. They heat fast and crisp well. Dual-basket models have two drawers you can run at different settings, so the main and side finish together. Oven-style air fryers have a door and racks or trays; they hold more and can toast and bake, but take more space and often cook a little slower.

3. Functions and temperature range

Every air fryer air fries. Roast, bake, reheat and broil are useful extras; dehydrate needs a low setting, around 105°F to 170°F, to dry fruit and jerky. Look for a top temperature of at least 400°F for crispy results.

4. Wattage and your outlet

Full-size air fryers usually draw about 1,500 to 1,800 watts and compact ones about 1,000 to 1,200. More power heats the basket faster. Plug a high-wattage model into its own outlet rather than sharing a circuit with a kettle or toaster.

5. Controls and presets

Dials are simple and quick; digital controls let you set exact temperatures and times, and presets cover common foods. Presets are starting points: most cooks end up setting the temperature and time themselves.

6. Cleaning and the nonstick coating

Choose a basket and crisper plate that are dishwasher safe. Most baskets have a nonstick coating, often ceramic; protect it by using wooden or silicone tools, and an oil mister instead of aerosol cooking spray.

7. Footprint and noise

Measure the space under your cabinets and leave room behind the air fryer, where it vents hot air. A fan is never silent, but some models are rated noticeably quieter than others.

Setting Up Your New Air Fryer: First-Use Tips

  1. Unpack everything, including any stickers, foam or cardboard inside the basket and under the crisper plate.
  2. Wash the basket and crisper plate in warm, soapy water and dry them well. Wipe the outside with a damp cloth.
  3. Find the right spot: a flat, heat-safe surface with the clearance your manual asks for around and behind the unit, away from the wall and not under a low cabinet.
  4. Do a first run empty if your manual recommends it, for about 10 minutes at 400°F. A slight smell the first time is normal as the coating cures.
  5. Start with an easy batch, such as frozen fries, to learn how fast your model cooks.

Converting Oven Recipes for Your New Air Fryer

Most recipes are still written for a regular oven. The rule of thumb for a conventional oven recipe is to set the air fryer 25°F lower and cook for about 20% less time, shaking or flipping halfway.

Air Fryer Recipes to Try First

A few easy recipes to get to know a new air fryer. Cook in a single layer and shake or flip halfway.

Crispy hand-cut french fries

Ingredients:

  • 2 large russet potatoes, cut into fries
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • Salt and pepper; optional garlic powder or paprika

Instructions:

  1. Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 30 minutes, then pat them very dry.
  2. Toss with the oil and seasoning.
  3. Preheat the air fryer to 375°F (190°C).
  4. Cook in a single layer for 15 to 20 minutes, shaking the basket halfway, until golden.
  5. Serve right away.

More tips in our air fryer french fries guide.

Crispy chicken wings

Ingredients:

  • 2 lb chicken wings, tips removed
  • 1 tablespoon aluminum-free baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon black pepper
  • Your favorite wing sauce

Instructions:

  1. Pat the wings dry with paper towels.
  2. Toss with the baking powder, salt and pepper.
  3. Preheat the air fryer to 400°F (205°C).
  4. Cook in a single layer for 20 to 25 minutes, flipping halfway, until the skin is crisp and the meat reaches at least 165°F (74°C).
  5. Toss with sauce and serve.

Apple chips

Ingredients:

  • 2 apples, cored and sliced very thin
  • Optional: cinnamon

Instructions:

  1. Arrange the slices in a single layer and sprinkle with cinnamon.
  2. Air fry at 300°F (150°C) for 15 to 20 minutes, flipping every 5 minutes, until the edges curl. They crisp further as they cool.
  3. With a dehydrate setting, dry them at about 135°F (57°C) for several hours instead.
  4. Cool completely and store airtight.

Sweet potato fries

Ingredients:

  • 2 medium sweet potatoes, cut into fries
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 teaspoon paprika and ½ teaspoon salt

Instructions:

  1. Toss the fries with the oil, paprika and salt.
  2. Preheat the air fryer to 375°F (190°C).
  3. Cook in a single layer for 15 to 18 minutes, shaking halfway.

Crispy tofu bites

Ingredients:

  • 1 block firm tofu, pressed and cubed
  • 1 tablespoon soy sauce
  • 1 teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil

Instructions:

  1. Marinate the tofu in the soy sauce and garlic powder for 15 minutes.
  2. Toss with the oil.
  3. Preheat the air fryer to 375°F (190°C).
  4. Cook for about 15 minutes, shaking gently halfway.
  5. Serve with a dipping sauce or in a salad.

Reheating leftovers

An air fryer reheats fried and crispy food far better than a microwave. Pizza slices and fries take about 3 to 5 minutes at 350°F (175°C); fried chicken takes about 8 to 10 minutes at 375°F (190°C), until it is hot in the middle.

Hungry for more? Try air fryer chicken breast or air fryer pork chops, and read can you put foil in an air fryer before you line the basket.

Important Note: Our Personal Experience

We want to assure you that all the air fryers featured in this article have been personally tested and used by us. Our reviews are based on real-world experience, not just product specifications. This way, you get honest insights and trusted recommendations to help you pick the best air fryer that fits your needs.

Air Fryer FAQ

What size air fryer do I need?

About 2 quarts for one person, 3 to 4 quarts for one to three people, 5 to 6 quarts for three to five, and 7 quarts or a dual-basket model for larger families.

Is an air fryer worth it?

For most households, yes: it crisps food with little oil, heats up faster than a full oven and is easy to clean. It is less useful if you mostly cook soups, stews or very large roasts.

Is the Instant Vortex the same as an Instant Pot?

No. The Instant Pot is a pressure cooker; the Vortex is the air fryer line from the same company. Some Instant Pot models take an air fryer lid or have one built in, like the Duo Crisp, but a dedicated air fryer such as the Vortex is simpler for everyday crisping.

How do I convert oven recipes to the air fryer?

Set the air fryer about 25°F lower and cook for about 20% less time than a conventional oven recipe. Our air fryer conversion calculator works it out for you.

Do I need to preheat an air fryer?

Many models cook better after 3 to 5 minutes of preheating; some, like the Philips XXL, are designed to need none. Follow your manual.

How much oil do I need?

A teaspoon to a tablespoon is usually enough, from an oil mister or tossed with the food. Frozen fries and nuggets need none.

Can I use parchment paper or foil in an air fryer?

Yes, if air can still move around the food: use perforated parchment, weigh it down with food, and never preheat with an empty liner. See foil in an air fryer.

How do I clean an air fryer?

Let it cool, wash the basket and crisper plate (most are dishwasher safe) and wipe the inside and outside with a damp cloth. Clean after each use so old grease doesn’t smoke.

Can I cook frozen fries in an air fryer?

Yes, straight from frozen and without extra oil. Most take about 12 to 15 minutes at 400°F, shaken every 5 minutes.

Final Verdict: The Best Air Fryer to Buy

  • Best Overall Ninja AF101 Air Fryer: simple, reliable and the right size for most kitchens.
  • Best for Families COSORI TurboBlaze 6-Quart Air Fryer: a large basket and up to 450°F for big batches.
  • Best for Instant Pot Fans Instant Vortex Plus 6-Quart Air Fryer: touchscreen programs from the makers of the Instant Pot.
  • Best Premium Philips Premium Airfryer XXL: family size with Fat Removal technology.
  • Best Budget Dash Compact Air Fryer: compact and affordable for one or two.
Our Top Recommendation

Ninja AF101 Air Fryer

For most people, we recommend the Ninja AF101. It covers air frying, roasting, reheating and dehydrating, cleans up in the dishwasher and fits on almost any counter.

Cooking for a bigger family? Step up to the COSORI TurboBlaze 6-Quart. Short on space or budget? The Dash Compact does the basics well.
